## D5 at a glance

- **Discrimination:** held-out AUC {{< var adj.auc >}} on the held-out
  {{< var adj.test_share >}} of applicants (bootstrap 95% interval
  {{< var adj.auc_ci_lo >}}–{{< var adj.auc_ci_hi >}}); lift {{< var adj.lift >}}× in the
  riskiest {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}} by PD.
- **Gates:** AUC ≥ {{< var adj.gate_auc >}} and lift ≥ {{< var adj.gate_lift >}}× on that
  population, asserted at training and recomputed by `verify.py` — both met.
- **On the loans the bank books:** held-out AUC {{< var adj.pop.booked.auc >}} on the
  {{< var adj.pop.booked.n >}} booked applicants in the held-out split — below the AUC gate
  value, and no better than the scorecard's {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} on the same rows; lift
  {{< var adj.pop.booked.lift >}}× still passes.
- **Mostly rules:** {{< var adj.decline.knockout_share >}} of held-out Declines carry a hard
  knockout. Adjudication is largely a rules engine with a model attached.
- **Six open findings** the chapter raises about its own model and policy
  ([5.7](limitations.qmd)).
:::

Loan Adjudication decides, for every applicant, Approve, Refer or Decline, with reasons
([5.1](purpose.qmd)). It is two components in sequence: a gradient-boosted model (LightGBM)
on {{< var adj.n_features >}} inputs — two of them the Business Credit Score's own output,
the score and its PD ([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd)) — and a policy layer of hard knockouts,
PD zones and refer overrides that turns the model's PD into the decision
([5.3](methodology.qmd)). It decides who gets credit, which makes it Tier 1
([D0](../d0-summary.qmd#risk-tiering)).

{{< include ../../_generated/adj-headline.md >}}

Measured on the held-out {{< var adj.test_share >}} of the {{< var adj.n_applicants >}}
applicants — the same rows as the scorecard's held-out split, drawn with the same seed and
stratification ([5.2](data.qmd#split-and-seed)).

The chapter follows the nine-part [template](../index.qmd#the-template), with D4 as the
worked example. Every number in it is a named fact, recomputed through the module's own
functions — the saved model, `compute_adjudication_features` and `policy.decide` — by
`python verify.py`; the [fact index](../../reference/facts.qmd) gives each one's source and
population. The chapter documents the model and policy as committed: it changes neither.
